messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am just starting to use the MSStats Skyline to perform label-based relative quantification. I went through the tutorials I could find and searched this group but could not find an example for a label-based workflow.

My samples consist of light cell lysates with heavy-labelled spike-in proteins. I would like to normalise my light cell lysate data based on the labelled proteins.
In the QC part, I understand that this is what a a median or quantile normalisation would do as they normalise reference intensities (maybe I have misunderstood what a "reference intensity means"). My question here is if I specify those reference intensities by setting the Sample Type to QC for those reference peptides? I assume the software will then know to use the labelled intensities as the reference?

In the Group Comparison part, I understand I should tick "Include reference standards" for my label-based normalisation. Firstly, does the same Sample Type>QC assign peptides as reference standards here? Secondly, for some reason the Group Comparison window does not show the "Include reference standards" (please see attachment). What could be the reason for this? I tried uninstalling and re-installing MSStats without any results.

I apologise if I have missed something completely.

Thanks a lot!
Kaspar

messages.subject: Re: Label-based QC and Group comparison in the Skyline tool
messages.subject_clean: Label-based QC and Group comparison in the Skyline tool
messages.body_plain:
Dear Kaspar,

If I understand correctly, your data set includes
     1) light intensities only for all proteins from cell lytes.
     2) light intensities + heavy intensity for spike in proteins

If correct, it is not label-based relative quantification on our side. label-based relative quantification should have all (or almost all) reference intensities of all proteins in your data. Then, there are two options for normalization.
  1) median normalization among all light intensities, remove reference intensities.
  2) global standard normalization with spike-in protein, remove reference intensities. How to set up those spike-in protein as standard is explained in the document (msstats.org <http://msstats.org> > msstats > documentation > Tutorial for msstats as external tool in Skyline, p2-3)

If not correct, here is my second guess.
   1) light intensities only for all proteins from cell lytes.
   2) heavy intensities only for spike-in proteins.
Then you want to used heavy intensities for spike-in proteins. We haven't tested these types of experiment. Technically, you can change the 'Label' for spike-in proteins as endogenous, then set up those proteins as standard and use global standard normalization.

'Include reference standards' option was removed. Skyline automatically reports heavy reference intensities as reference. Those were for remove all reference intensities for label-based quantification. But, it was not much useful and made more confused. So, we moved these option.

It seems that we need to clarify some terminology. 'reference' is the same as isotope-labelled heavy peptide. spike-in proteins for quality control is called 'global standard or normalization standard'.

And MSstats does not use 'QC' information from Type in Skyline.

Hope to help.
- Meena

messages.subject: Re: Heatmap Error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Zack,

If you use group comparison of msstat in Skyline, you can compare only one comparison a try. If there is only one comparison, heatmap will not be drawn. If you use multiple groups, the comparison will compare between average of multiple groups vs control group. For example, you select group1 as control group, and select group2 and 3 for comparison, the result will be (group2+group3)/2 vs group1. You can see it in 'label' column in testingresult.csv and the title of volcano plot.

If you want to compare multiple comparison together and draw the heatmap, I recommend to use R directly.

- Meena

messages.body_plain:
Then, what I understand is.

Let's assume that there are 1300 proteins from cell lyte.
1) light intensities for 1280 proteins + 20 proteins
2) heavy intensities for 20 proteins.

which means that there are light and heavy intensities for 20 proteins in your data. (because you said 20 from 1300)

'global standards' means the endogenous (light) proteins which should be constant across samples. If you assign 20 proteins as global standards in Skyline, that means those 20 endogenous proteins should be constant across samples and global standard normalization method uses light intensities values of 20 proteins for normalization.

Heavy intensities can't be used as global standards. If there are heavy intensities in your data, equalized median or quantile normalization in MSstats use reference intensities. So, if you select equalize median or quantile normalization, it will use heavy intensities of 20 proteins only. But, I'm not sure whether your data can pass all data checking procedure in MSstats or not. If it works, you can check from QC plots. Otherwise, it seems that some extra processing in R, with MSstats report from Skyline will be necessary.

- Meena
